body.statement: As a required reduction, suppose exactly one hazard may depend on a substantive state: \(S_k=\{j\}\), where \(j\in\{k,k+1\}\), and \(S_t=\varnothing\) for \(t\ne k\). Then \(\mathsf C=1\) if and only if there are \(d<k\) and \(\ell\ge j\) with \(\ell\in B_d\). The minimal frontier consists exactly of the singleton designs \(B_d=\{\ell\}\) with all other bundles empty and \(d<k\le j\le\ell\).
body.justification: This arbitrary-horizon reduction forces the general calculus to reproduce a tractable boundary and its positive gamma-swap obstruction.
body.gap: The anchor proves passive nonidentification along a self-censoring path but does not state when a downstream audit destroys the cancellation or enumerate minimal audits.
body.consumer: It gives a closed-form measurement rule when scientific knowledge isolates one informative dropout hazard.
